stories.name: Microsoft stock surge
stories.blurb: Microsoft shares are climbing sharply as analysts raise price targets and the company posts strong earnings driven by Azure growth.

stories.name: Enterprise Tech Market Reports
stories.blurb: A series of market research reports projecting growth in enterprise IT sectors like cloud, AI, quantum computing, and digital transformation, with Microsoft named among the leading vendors.

stories.name: ETF Investing Guides
stories.blurb: A collection of articles offering advice and comparisons on ETFs for dividends, long-term growth, and passive income.

stories.name: Big Tech AI Spending Concerns
stories.blurb: Investors and credit markets are increasingly scrutinizing whether the massive, escalating capital expenditures by Microsoft and other hyperscalers on AI infrastructure are financially sustainable.

stories.name: Enterprise Software Stock Valuations
stories.blurb: A series of analyses examining whether enterprise software and cybersecurity stocks like Salesforce, CrowdStrike, Oracle, Palo Alto Networks, and UiPath are fairly valued given their growth prospects

rel.why: Stock commentary on Salesforce, UiPath, and CrowdStrike; no bearing on Microsoft itself or its close ecosystem.

stories.name: IREN Microsoft Deal
stories.blurb: IREN's multibillion-dollar cloud computing partnership with Microsoft and whether the company can execute on its ambitious AI data center buildout.

rel.why: IREN is a Microsoft AI cloud partner/counterparty, so its AI datacenter capacity, pricing, and contract growth bear on Microsoft's cloud supply and competitive

stories.name: Microsoft green card suspension
stories.blurb: The Trump administration suspended Microsoft from a green card labor program over alleged H-1B visa abuse, drawing sharp criticism from Vice President Vance and a response from the company.

past.name: Microsoft Earnings Optimism
past.blurb: Analysts and investors express strong bullish sentiment on Microsoft stock ahead of and following its July 29 earnings report, predicting significant gains.

past.name: Microsoft Xbox Layoffs
past.blurb: Microsoft is cutting thousands of jobs, with the Xbox gaming division hit hardest as the company restructures its game studios and workforce.

past.name: AI Safety and Regulation
past.blurb: OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI labs are navigating safety testing, government oversight, and internal tensions as they race to release increasingly powerful models.

past.name: AI in advertising
past.blurb: Microsoft leaders and other tech executives discuss how AI is reshaping digital advertising and why most current ads perform poorly.

past.name: AI Infrastructure Boom
past.blurb: Coverage of the surge in AI data-center investment and deals—like Nscale's IPO and Nvidia's backing of Anthropic—highlighting Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon, and others racing to secure AI compute capacity

past.name: Meta's AI Cloud Push
past.blurb: Meta is reportedly building a new cloud computing business to sell excess AI compute capacity, positioning itself to compete with Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet in cloud services.

Alphabet Q2 earnings show AI spending surge
Nebius raises $775M debt for AI cloud

Microsoft expands AMD Azure AI deal
Trump hosts White House AI meeting
Microsoft unveils Nvidia-powered Surface Laptop Ultra
US suspends Microsoft from green card program

14.text: Microsoft neared a $4 trillion valuation after a Melius Research upgrade, and analysts including Jim Cramer called it a top AI winner as Copilot momentum and infrastructure spending grew. It unveiled an Nvidia-powered Surface Laptop Ultra with on-device AI, launched Muse for Windows, and Satya Nadella urged emergency brake controls on advanced AI.

6.text: RegASK and Digitate expanded availability and partnerships via Microsoft Marketplace and a Microsoft partnership, while LocalStack launched an Azure local-cloud beta. Multiple market reports (quantum, data virtualization, IT operations, change management) list Microsoft among key vendors, with no Microsoft-specific news.

16.text: Microsoft is only mentioned incidentally as a holding in broad ETFs like VUG, VIG, and MOAT; the articles focus on ETF performance, fees, and dividend strategies rather than any Microsoft-specific news.

5.text: Big Tech’s AI spending is increasingly debt-financed, with AI-related borrowing at 25% of corporate bond issuance versus 4% two years ago, while free cash flow turns negative. Ray Dalio and Michael Burry warn the AI bubble is near bursting; Bank of America raised its Big Tech capex forecast past $1 trillion, with Microsoft among top spenders.

12.text: IREN is shifting its Bitcoin data-center capacity to AI cloud computing and reportedly signed a multi-year Anthropic cloud contract, sending its stock up. The other articles cover AI cloud competitors CoreWeave and Nebius; Microsoft is barely mentioned.

15.text: The U.S. Labor Department suspended Microsoft, Adobe, and other tech firms from the PERM green card certification program, citing abuse, with Microsoft pushing back. The same day, Trump awarded Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella a national science medal, while JD Vance defended the crackdown.

4.text: Azure passed $100 billion in annual revenue and posted 43% growth, with strong AI demand lifting Microsoft shares 41% over six months. Analysts remain largely bullish, though the stock trades below its 52-week high at about 29 times earnings, above Alphabet, Amazon, and Salesforce.

7.text: OpenAI and Anthropic are hiring politically experienced staff as AI becomes a national security issue, and Anthropic expanded its cyber verification program. Trump will reportedly award Musk, Huang, and Nadella the nation's top science and tech medals.

9.text: The Trump administration suspended Microsoft from the PERM green card program, accusing it of displacing American workers with H-1B visa holders; JD Vance publicly pressed the claim, and Microsoft denied underpaying visa staff. Separately, Xbox formed a media division to license game franchises and pursued GTA VI streaming rights.
